content: Type 1 Diabetes is a chronic autoimmune condition characterized by the destruction of insulin-producing beta cells in the pancreas, leading to absolute insulin deficiency. The American Diabetes Association (ADA) provides guidelines and recommendations for the diagnosis, management, and treatment of diabetes, including Type 1 Diabetes. In Type 2 Diabetes, there is emerging evidence suggesting that autoimmunity may play a role in certain subsets of patients, although it is traditionally considered a metabolic disorder. Patients receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, a class of cancer immunotherapy drugs, may experience immune-related adverse reactions. These reactions are more likely to occur in individuals who carry high-risk HLA-DR4 alleles, which are associated with increased susceptibility to autoimmune conditions.
